Primary request: Make a new present-day documentary photograph of the real Kerimäki Church and its separate bell tower in Savonlinna. Reproduce the architecture from both verified reference photographs, especially the church's cruciform timber mass, yellow-and-white boarded façades, Gothic-pattern windows, broad dark pitched roofs, the tall rounded GREEN COPPER central dome with its small white lantern and cross, and the separate tall yellow-and-white bell tower with its dark stone lower section. Show enough of the church behind it to communicate its large cross-shaped mass, but do not invent unseen wings.
Style/medium: natural unedited-looking architectural photograph from an everyday full-frame camera, moderate lens, normal optical perspective.
Lighting/mood: plain Finnish summer daylight with some light cloud, restrained contrast, ordinary shadow detail.
Materials/textures: believable painted timber with small age variation, real green oxidized copper dome, irregular stone masonry on bell tower base, ordinary grass and trees; moderate sharpness without microcontrast.
Constraints: preserve the exact current architecture in the two references. The church central dome must be green copper, tall and rounded, not black, not a shallow mansard or onion dome. The detached bell tower must not merge into the church. No construction scene, historic costumes, crowds, scaffolding, text, logos or watermark. Avoid CGI-clean surfaces, HDR, painterly treatment, dramatic sky, perfect symmetry, oversaturation and invented architectural ornament.

Constraints: no bridge, dam, castle, cathedral, Alps, boats, people, signs, readable text, logos or watermark. No historical reconstruction. Do not widen the river into a lake or invent cliffs.
